title: Varnode::getLocalType full port: typelock early return, def outputTypeLocal seed, stop_type_propagation early return with blockup, descend insertion-order typeOrder-min merge with first-encountered tie survival, and the NULL local type LowlevelError channel
status_note: Production commit 8c26662 ports Varnode::getLocalType (varnode.cc:900-936) in full, replacing the v_type-clone stub, plus the op.hh:251-252 outputTypeLocal/inputTypeLocal dispatch table and the varnode addl_flags STOP_UP_PROPAGATION=0x800/HAS_IMPLIED_FIELD=0x1000 constants with stops/set/clear accessors. The locked Ghidra 12.0.4 oracle and the frozen Rugra snapshot were each executed twice with deterministic stdout/stderr. Both sides produced 62 records / 2194 bytes with identical sha256 and empty stderr; the bilateral byte diff is empty (exit 0). Re-pinned 2026-08-25 from base 8c26662 to 5cba7550 (TYPEOP-LOCALTYPE-CALLOTHER-0001 userops parameter thread; fixture call sites pass None, zero behavior drift, locked capture unchanged). All eleven cases match: def_only (int4 via TypeOpPtrsub::getOutputLocal getBase(4,TYPE_INT)), def_stop (STOP early return: blockup=1, uint reader never consulted, int4 kept), def_nostop (uint4 replaces int4 via SUB_UINT_PLAIN < SUB_INT_PLAIN), readers_min in both insertion orders (uint4 regardless of order), ptr_pointee_replace (int4* strictly smaller than char* through the TypePointer::compare pointee descent, type.cc:951), tie_structs_ab / tie_structs_ba (two distinct empty structures have TypeStruct::compare == 0 at level 10, type.cc:1742-1780; the first-encountered struct survives both orderings), path_beats_int (char* SUB_PTR beats int8 SUB_INT_PLAIN), typelock_union (locked union returned directly, def and reader never consulted), null_local_type (LowlevelError "NULL local type" observed as an in-fixture caught record with blockup staying false).

decisive_semantics.references_and_outputs: blockup is a reference out-parameter that getLocalType only ever sets to true (cc:913) and never clears; the caller initializes it to false per varnode (coreaction.cc:5020). The return Datatype* is the factory-canonical object (repeat calls preserve pointer identity, verified by repeat_identity); a type-locked varnode returns its locked type without touching blockup; the all-null path throws LowlevelError("NULL local type") (cc:934), observed as an in-fixture caught record on both sides.
decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_and_order: The descendant walk is the raw std::list addDescend insertion order (cc:921) — no sorting, no skipping; the slot is op->getSlot(this), the first inrefs pointer-identity match (op.hh:166). The fixture pins both insertion orders for the uint/int competition and both orderings of the struct tie, proving order sensitivity is exactly first-encountered survival on ties.
decisive_semantics.counters_and_accumulators: No counters. The accumulator ct starts as def->outputTypeLocal() (cc:911) or null and is replaced only when 0 > newct->typeOrder(*ct) (cc:929) — strictly smaller wins: submeta ascending, size descending (type.cc:212-218), with TypePointer::compare pointee descent (type.cc:951) and TypeStruct::compare field tables (type.cc:1742-1780).
decisive_semantics.sort_and_comparison_keys: typeOrder = pointer-equality shortcut 0, else compare(op,10): submeta ascending (SUB_PARTIALUNION=0 .. SUB_VOID=23, type.hh:103-128), then size descending. Ties keep the incumbent; the def's type is the incumbent for every descendant comparison.
